assignment: A declared script or tool owns at least one result.

rules.instruction: Mechanical responsibility applies only to the specifically assigned result owned by a declared script or tool. That tool owns its preflight, internal commands, generated output and errors. Use only its documented inputs, output and exit status. Run it once. When the Host returns a completed job whose exit status is the result, cite its job ID, status, exit code, signal and log reference without reopening or copying the log. On zero exit, accept the tool-owned result as complete without auditing or rerunning it; continue only separately assigned work outside the tool, or report success and stop when none remains. On nonzero exit, report the original error and stop. Do not investigate, decompose, supplement or recheck the tool. Repository lint, compilation, build and unit-test entrypoints used to validate directly authored code are development feedback rather than tool-owned deliverables. When a development responsibility is also assigned, inspect their failure output and make a cause-directed code correction under that responsibility.
